evaluation.note: On the Genealogy of Morality, Preface. Public domain. The passage is chosen because it genuinely supports every reference concept: it names the value judgments good and evil and asks under what conditions they arose. An earlier draft used a passage that supported none of them, and the live evaluation is what caught it.
evaluation.text: Under what conditions did man construct for himself those judgments of value, good and evil? And what intrinsic worth do they possess in themselves? My curiosity and my suspicions halted betimes at the question of what origin our terms good and evil actually have. The problem of the origin of morality, and of the value of our morality itself, is the problem I set myself: to traverse the immense, distant, and concealed land of morality, and to discover the conditions and circumstances out of which these values grew.
